summary: Mashable's Black Friday 2023 roundup of 200+ Walmart deals across categories such as TVs, laptops, headphones, gaming, vacuums, kitchen, outdoor, Apple, pets, fitness and toys. It explains Walmart's sale timing (online first, stores opening Nov. 24 at 6 a.m.) and announces an early Cyber Monday sale for Walmart+ members. Each category highlights a featured deal with reasons it is worthwhile.
one_line: Mashable's guide to Walmart's 2023 Black Friday and early Cyber Monday deals, with featured picks across tech, home, fitness and toys.
key_facts: Walmart launched its first round of Black Friday deals on Nov. 8, 2023, and the last round of online rollbacks went live Wednesday, Nov. 22 at 3 p.m. ET.
Walmart stores opened to in-person Black Friday shoppers on Friday, Nov. 24 at 6 a.m., with shopping lasting until 11 p.m.; hours can vary by location.
Walmart's Cyber Monday sale starts Sunday, Nov. 26 at 7 p.m. ET on Walmart.com and the Walmart app, with up to 80% off apparel, beauty, tech, toys and more.
Walmart+ members get Cyber Monday access three hours early, at 4 p.m. ET, for the first time ever for that sale.
The second-gen AirPods Pro with Lightning port cost $169 at Walmart, their lowest price to date; Amazon had never gone below $189.
The Xbox Series X bundle with Diablo IV was $439, an all-time low, versus the console's usual $499.99 on its own; Xbox Wire had pegged the Microsoft Store price at $509.99.
The Apple Watch Series 9 (45mm GPS) was $359, an all-time low at Walmart; it has an s9 chip about 30 percent faster and double peak brightness.
The Echelon Connect Sport bike, a Walmart-exclusive Peloton alternative, was $297, over $400 off, with 32 levels of magnetic resistance and a 30-day free Echelon Premier trial.
The JBL portable Bluetooth speaker was $89 at Walmart, versus a $179.95 retail price on JBL's website; it is IPX7-rated for waterproofing.
Dyson's V15 Detect Absolute vacuum was 27% off, making it $100 cheaper than the Dyson V12 Detect Slim.
The Tractive dog tracker was $29.99, saving $20, and the onn. tablet was in the $20 range, while Fire tablets only fell to $40.
A LEGO Star Wars kit of The Child (Baby Yoda) was discounted 50%, which the article notes is rare as the era of doorbuster deals is ending.
